subject: maths
question:
Evaluate the following.

sin 25° sin 65° – cos 25° cos 65°.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the complementary angle properties: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Substitute 65° = 90° − 25° in the given expression:

sin 25° sin(90° − 25°) − cos 25° cos(90° − 25°)

This simplifies directly to: sin 25° cos 25° − cos 25° sin 25° = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: sin 25° sin 65° − cos 25° cos 65°

**Formula Used:**

cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B

**Calculation:**

⇒ The given expression can be written as:

⇒ −(cos 25° cos 65° − sin 25° sin 65°)

⇒ Using the formula cos(A + B) = cos A cos B − sin A sin B:

⇒ −cos(25° + 65°)

⇒ −cos(90°)

⇒ We know that cos 90° = 0.

⇒ −0 = 0.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Addition Identities

cos(A − B) = cos A cos B + sin A sin B

sin(A + B) = sin A cos B + cos A sin B

sin(A − B) = sin A cos B − cos A sin B

Complementary Angles

Angles whose sum is 90° are complementary. sin(90° − θ) = cos θ and cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Values of Standard Angles

sin 90° = 1, cos 90° = 0, tan 90° is Not Defined.
